method: Before reading the subject, derived four falsifiers for an altitude correction: it must classify by decision consequence rather than document syntax; retain every load-bearing invariant or explicitly rehome it; preserve open-finding/status traceability; and bind future detailed design back to architectural counterexamples.
Diffed the D9 extraction against architecture/07, d9-exit-contract.v1.5 invariants/class semantics, versioning-policy.v1, and both v1.5 reviews.

Diffed the R-1 extraction against architecture/08, r1-lifetime-neutrality.conformance.v1.3, the v1.2/v1.3 B reviews, and A1 confirmations, focusing on boundary and authority rather than API field lists.
Audited cross-document authority after the register rebind: architecture binding prose, register bindingArtifact/validator, claim dependencies, and METHOD.ALTITUDE status presentation.
Did not use the subject's detail percentages as corroboration; construct validity of that instrument is itself under review.
whatCouldHaveFailed: The altitude correction could be directionally right but use an invalid percentage metric to ratify unrelated artifacts.
Demoting wire detail could also demote a public consumer-custody contract or a component boundary that is architectural.
The D9/R-1 extraction could silently omit invariants found during detailed review.
A candidate method rule could be presented as SEALED or used to rebind claims before review.
The old checkers could remain advertised as validators for new binding artifacts they do not inspect.

acceptedDirection: Architecture should bind invariants, responsibility boundaries, ownership, consequences, alternatives, and falsifying counterexamples rather than accidental field spellings.
A detailed conformance exploration may remain useful without being the architecture decision itself.
D9 and R-1 consumed disproportionate effort on author-controlled schemas/checkers; stopping further version churn pending architectural review is prudent.
The artifact honestly admits that its percentage proxy is crude and that extraction by the original author is conflict-prone.
positiveAssessment.notAccepted: The current metric, categorical method rule, D9 extraction, R-1 extraction, and register rebindings are not adequate binding replacements.

findings.title: METHOD.ALTITUDE was restated inside a SEALED method container while the register called it CANDIDATE
evidence: claim-register METHOD.ALTITUDE is CANDIDATE and initially had no restatements
architecture/10 labels Method rules SEALED, then states the corrected rule under heading 3 without an inline candidate mark
the canonical checker reported 31 claims clean because the restatement was absent from the register
findings.impact: The artifact created the exact status-promotion failure its altitude correction is meant to prevent, while the status checker stayed green.
findings.requiredChange: Register the architecture/10 restatement and mark METHOD.ALTITUDE CANDIDATE inline. This presentation repair was applied during review; it does not accept the rule's substance.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: Evidence that the SEALED marker did not govern method rule 3 or that the register already tracked an inline downgrade; neither was true.

findings.title: Unreproducible detail percentages are used to ratify six unrelated artifacts and an unexplained 24% threshold
evidence: measurement.method names broad categories but supplies no byte counts, classifier, denominator, script, ambiguity policy, or per-artifact derivation
c2-plan-stage-schema is called 'mixed, acceptable' at 24% without a threshold or decision-based criterion
whatDoesNotChange promotes threat, operability, versioning, delivery, resolved-inputs, and fact-identity as acceptable altitude from this proxy
knownLimitations admits a short invariant can matter more than a long schema, defeating percentage as the classification instrument
findings.impact: A local document-shape estimate silently becomes a global architecture judgment. The same metric could bless an implementation decision written in prose or reject an architectural public contract expressed as a schema.
findings.requiredChange: Withdraw the percentages as decision evidence. Audit each artifact by the consequence, custody, ownership, external compatibility, and reversibility of the decision it makes. If percentages remain descriptive, publish reproducible raw counts and state that they decide nothing.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A reproducible classifier validated against independently labelled architectural/detail decisions and a justified decision threshold; none is provided.

findings.title: The corrected method overcorrects: a schema or hash choice can itself be architectural
evidence: rootCause.correctedRule says an architectural decision closes 'not with a schema' and that needing field names, enums, or hashes proves mis-scoping
D9 exit classes/codes are explicitly CONSUMER-CUSTODY in versioning-policy.v1 because build scripts cannot negotiate them
cross-process, cross-version, persisted, or public contracts can make an exact discriminant, identity algorithm, or compatibility rule the high-cost architectural boundary
findings.impact: The rule substitutes one syntactic heuristic for another. It can erase necessary public compatibility decisions merely because their most precise expression is a schema.
findings.requiredChange: Define altitude by blast radius, external custody, ownership boundary, reversibility, and change cost. A schema is detailed when it merely implements a chosen boundary; it is architectural when its exact compatibility semantics are the boundary. Keep architecture and conformance as separately reviewable layers linked by mandatory traceability.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A definition of architecture that intentionally excludes public/persisted interface contracts; that would conflict with this project's compatibility and baseline obligations.

findings.title: The D9 extraction loses the semantic remedy partition and multiple architectural failure invariants
evidence: TO-1 says one total union but does not bind the six remedy meanings; TO-7 forbids two remedies behind one code without defining the remedies; TO-8 makes an unspecified set additive
architecture/07 and d9 v1.5 distinguish success, policy failure, request rejection, indeterminate, operational failure, and interruption because collapsing them changes CI action

the extraction omits envelope/process termination parity, pre-admission failure constructibility, policy-not-Error and operational-not-Finding separation, orphan-publication recovery, exit-zero-not-attestation, tombstone-backed expiry, and the baseline no-mass-net-new prohibited effect
the demoted artifact's own invariant list contains these obligations, and prior reviews treated several as load-bearing rather than field-shape detail
findings.impact: An implementation can satisfy TO-1..TO-8 with one generic failure class, no pre-admission representation, no envelope parity, and no orphan/baseline safety. The extraction is too weak to replace D9 as architecture.
findings.requiredChange: Produce a D9 architecture v2 that binds the semantic remedy partition and every retained failure-safety invariant, or explicitly rehomes each with a referenced claim. Keep exact payload fields separate, but keep the public class/code compatibility contract binding somewhere rather than NON-BINDING.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A trace showing every omitted invariant is sealed under another claim and that the six remedy semantics remain binding through a referenced consumer contract.

findings.title: TO-8 imports an unsettled versioning decision without dependency or ownership
evidence: TO-8 asserts the exit class set is additive-only permanently
that rule lives in candidate VERSIONING V4, whose decision dependencies include D9 and whose own review has open blockers
D9 dependsOn remains empty, so the extraction presents the imported policy as a self-contained D9 invariant
additive-only does not by itself specify how old consumers handle a new class or prevent semantic reassignment of existing scenarios
findings.impact: D9 can appear closable while relying on an unsettled, potentially circular compatibility policy. A permanent product contract is introduced without its decision source or consumer behavior.
findings.requiredChange: Assign class-set evolution to VERSIONING and reference it as an explicit dependency, or make it a D9-owned decision and remove the reverse dependency. Bind existing class/code meanings against renumbering/repurposing and separately decide compatible addition behavior.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A sealed product decision already owning additive-only exit evolution with defined old-consumer behavior.

findings.title: R-1 demotes the execution-core boundary even though the corrected method names boundaries as architecture
evidence: EC-1 refers to 'the execution core' but r1_executionCore defines no inside/outside ownership boundary
EC-1 infers lifetime neutrality from nothing in the surface distinguishing lifetimes, repeating the local-form-to-global-property error
B-R1V12-03 and A1-R1V13-03 remain open on whether providers/Probes execute outside through observations/supervision or inside through a registry with ambient compiler authority
EC-4/EC-5 pull storage-protocol obligations into the R-1 set while cancellation, telemetry neutrality, effectful-stage placement, and host/core publication ownership are omitted or unassigned
findings.impact: There is no stable subject for EC-1/EC-7 and no way to determine which behavior must be lifetime-neutral. A surface can omit an isResident flag while linked providers, globals, cancellation, or publication still make semantics lifetime-dependent.
findings.requiredChange: Retain an architecture-level core/host/provider/storage boundary without choosing an API signature or CoreDeps fields. State semantic re-entrancy and cancellation/progress parity, place effectful stages and publication, reference storage invariants rather than absorbing them, and add falsifying counterexamples.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A separately binding boundary artifact that defines the core and resolves effectful provider placement, referenced by R-1.

findings.title: EC-7 repeats the absolute ambient-authority claim despite known closure limits and a reopened capability substrate
evidence: EC-7 says the core holds no ambient authority and that closure analysis plus runtime denial establishes absence

B-R1V12-02/05 and A1-R1V13-02/03 show store/provider ports, dynamic loading, FFI/native code, injected implementations, and unexecuted branches make that global conclusion either impossible or vacuous without a declared boundary
ARCH.PROBE-CONTRACT is REOPENED specifically because runtime-closure review found linked TCB code retains ambient authority and no denial substrate is designed
R-1 dependsOn is empty and its new seal blockers omit the capability-boundary findings
findings.impact: The extraction promotes a disputed capability claim while dropping the findings that falsified its earlier form. An injected interface or passing representative runtime test can again be mistaken for absence of authority.
findings.requiredChange: Narrow EC-7 to a declared static/runtime boundary: direct core modules cannot reach ambient authority; named adapter/provider implementations are explicit TCB or OS-confined capabilities with separate tests. State dynamic/native coverage limits and record the ARCH.PROBE dependency until the denial model is resolved.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A complete construction that denies dynamic/native/adapter ambient access at runtime and a closure model proven complete for the shipped execution boundary.

findings.title: Rebinding D9 and R-1 drops open review findings without disposition or rehoming
evidence: scope-correction has no resolves map for B-D9V15-01..05, A1 D9 findings, B-R1V12-02..07, B-R1V13-01/02, or A1 R1 findings
whatDoesNotChange merely says the defects were real, without classifying them as architectural, detailed-design, superseded, or owned elsewhere
the register replaced explicit D9 and R-1 blockers with generic invariant-review lines; critical capability, provider-boundary, identity, return-contract, and checker defects disappeared
the subject's own known limitation says extraction by the original author is least likely to notice a dropped invariant
findings.impact: Open findings are effectively laundered out of the authoritative status surface by changing the binding object. Future reviewers are told only to check TO/EC completeness without knowing which rejected guarantees must survive or which detailed contract remains unsafe.
findings.requiredChange: A v2 must carry a per-finding disposition: retained architectural invariant, rehomed claim/dependency, detailed-design blocker, superseded with reason, or still open. Restore all unresolved architectural findings to register blockers until independently discharged.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A separate authoritative disposition artifact already linked from every affected register entry.

findings.title: D9 prose, register, and validator now name three different authorities while the checker reports clean
evidence: architecture/07 still says d9-exit-contract.v1.5 is the binding artifact and check-d9 D1..D10 is retained
the register binds scope-correction-a3.v1#d9_terminationOutcome
the same register retains validator=check-d9.py even though scope-correction says that checker is not an architecture gate and the checker defaults to v1.4
check-claims reports CHK-0..CHK-5 clean because its version-drift logic cannot relate differently named binding artifacts
findings.impact: A reader, an agent, and the canonical command receive different answers about what D9 means and what has been validated. This is a real clean-checker/false-authority violation.
findings.requiredChange: Choose one current architectural binding, update architecture/07 and the register atomically, and classify check-d9 only as the validator of a named non-binding detailed contract. Extend status integrity later only if it can check semantic binding aliases without more allowlist heuristics.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A documented two-layer authority model already distinguishing architectural binding from detailed-contract validator in both prose and register; none is present.

findings.title: Demoted specifications are non-binding, but no rule requires future design to inherit the extracted invariants
evidence: D9 and R-1 extraction lists invariants but no falsifying counterexamples or acceptance-test handoff
whatChanges says old checkers are not architecture gates and no more spec versions should be produced yet
nothing requires a future production contract to trace TO/EC invariants or independently retest the defects found in prior rounds
A1-RTV4-01 identified and repaired the same gap for retention v4
findings.impact: The next detailed contract can satisfy its own schema while silently dropping an extracted invariant, recreating Error 6 at a new layer.
findings.requiredChange: Give every retained invariant at least one falsifying counterexample and require future detailed contracts to trace each invariant/counterexample to independent acceptance evidence or a reviewed structural-impossibility argument.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A mandatory cross-layer traceability rule already applying to TO/EC with independently owned negative cases.

resolves.B-SC-01: PRESENTATION-FIX-APPLIED: METHOD.ALTITUDE restatement registered and marked CANDIDATE inline; substantive review remains open.
resolves.B-SC-02: OPEN-BLOCKER: detail percentages cannot classify artifact altitude or ratify six artifacts.
resolves.B-SC-03: OPEN-BLOCKER: method rule must classify by consequence/custody/boundary rather than forbid schema-shaped architecture categorically.
resolves.B-SC-04: OPEN-BLOCKER: D9 extraction loses semantic classes and multiple architectural invariants.
resolves.B-SC-05: OPEN-BLOCKER: TO-8 has hidden candidate VERSIONING ownership/dependency and undefined compatible addition behavior.
resolves.B-SC-06: OPEN-BLOCKER: R-1 extraction has no execution-core boundary and EC-1 mistakes surface shape for semantic neutrality.
resolves.B-SC-07: OPEN-BLOCKER: EC-7 overclaims absence of ambient authority and omits the reopened capability dependency.
resolves.B-SC-08: OPEN-BLOCKER: prior open findings were dropped from binding status without per-finding dispositions.
resolves.B-SC-09: OPEN-BLOCKER: architecture prose, register binding, and validator disagree on D9 authority while canonical checks pass.
resolves.B-SC-10: OPEN-BLOCKER: no mandatory invariant/counterexample handoff to future detailed design.

sealedPropertiesCovered: architecture/10 method rule 4 — artifacts must back-reference the decisions they encode
architecture/10 method rule 7 — do not use an unreviewed claim as a settled premise
architecture/10 method rule 8 — status attaches to claims, not containers
architecture/07 — termination semantic classes, one host mapper, publication/finalization safety, and public parity
architecture/08 R-1 — lifetime neutrality is semantic and separable from residency product decisions
architecture/02 — ExecutionId is host-admission attempt identity and telemetry is never evidence
architecture/03 — cancellation and storage integrity boundaries
ARCH.PROBE-CONTRACT reopened finding — an interface/signature is not a capability boundary
VERSIONING candidate — public exit classes/codes are consumer-custody compatibility artifacts
knownLimitations: This review does not produce the required scope-correction v2 or choose the final D9/R-1 invariant sets.

It does not independently classify every threat, operability, versioning, delivery, resolved-inputs, fact-identity, or C2 statement by altitude; it rejects the subject's categorical pass because the percentage instrument cannot do that work.

It relies on prior retained D9/R-1 review artifacts for detailed counterexamples and independently checks whether their architectural force survived extraction; it does not re-run all 39 D9 cases or an unimplemented R1 suite.
No implementation source was inspected because the subject makes greenfield architecture and method claims, not claims about current runtime behavior.
The METHOD.ALTITUDE status-label repair was applied during review, so reproducing B-SC-01 requires the recorded pre-fix state in this artifact and prior register/log history.
confidence: high on status, extraction loss, dependency, and authority findings; medium-high on the exact eventual allocation of public D9 compatibility semantics between architecture and versioning.
sealRecommendation: Do not seal METHOD.ALTITUDE, D9, or R-1 from scope-correction-a3.v1. Accept the direction, reject the current metric and extractions, restore finding traceability, and require independent review of a decision-based v2 before rebinding architecture authority.
